title: Stability lane bill-of-support and upgrade advisor
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Goal: Create a single, actionable 'bill-of-support' per stability lane (Stability, LTS, and Maintenance) that maps component compatibility windows (runtime, API, client SDKs, console) and wire an 'Upgrade Advisor' into the Console to drive safe, low-effort rollouts. This ticket defines the matrix format, compatibility contract language, rollout gate semantics, and an initial implementation plan for the advisor rules engine and UI hooks.

Scope:
- Define per-component support windows (patch/major/compat) and deprecation timelines for the three lanes.
- Produce a machine-readable support manifest that can be consumed by CI, the Console, and CLI upgrade tooling.
- Specify rollout gate types (canary %, health checks, evals, automatic rollback triggers) and the advisor decision logic.
- Implement a minimal advisor prototype in Console that recommends canary percentages and fallback targets for runtime/API/SDK upgrades.
- Create migration playbooks for common incompatibilities (tokenization, kernel ABI, API param changes).

Out of scope for this ticket: full automation of cross-cluster upgrades and on-prem packaged upgrade agents; these will be follow-ups after the manifest and advisor primitives are validated.
acceptance_criteria: Support manifest schema v1 defined and checked into repo (YAML + JSON Schema)
Per-component support windows documented for runtime, API, SDKs, and console in the manifest
Console advisor prototype surfaces a recommended rollout plan for at least one LTS -> stable upgrade path
CI step validates manifest format and fails PRs that would widen incompatibility beyond declared windows
Migration playbook draft for runtime ABI changes published in Confluence
Stakeholders (Runtime, API, SDK, Console, Product) have signed off on compatibility contract wording
progress_updates: 2025-02-18: Ticket created after cross-team planning sync. Initial scope and owners assigned.
2025-02-21: Draft manifest schema sketched (fields: component, lane, supported_versions, incompatible_until, deprecation_date, migration_notes). Shared with Runtime and SDK leads for feedback.
2025-02-25: Runtime team provided compatibility matrix for kernel and KV cache ABI; identified two fields that require explicit migration steps (KV cache format, kv_cache_v2 flag).
2025-02-28: Console team started UI mock for Upgrade Advisor; Early sketch recommends canary 5%-20% with health SLO pass threshold 99.5% over 5 minutes.

2025-03-03: Prototype manifest schema v1 checked into GitHub (link in links). Advisor prototype can read manifest and generate a human-readable plan in Console. Seeking design and security review before merging to main.
decisions: Use a lane-first manifest approach (lanes: Stability, LTS, Maintenance) rather than per-version-only metadata to simplify policy reasoning.

Semantic versioning policy: runtime and SDKs will promise minor-version backward compatibility for the current lane and one prior minor; API will maintain request/response schema compatibility for the lane unless explicitly marked as breaking in the manifest.
Rollout gates: Canary percentage, health SLO check, model-evaluation (for serving regressions), and automatic fallback target are the minimal gate set for v1.
Manifest format: YAML primary, JSON Schema for validation, stored in release-engineering repo under /manifests/lane-support/.
Advisor surface: Read-only recommendations in console for v1; no automatic execution of rollouts in this ticket. Automation is a follow-up after 2 release cycles.
open_questions: How long should deprecation windows be for language-model runtime internals (recommended: 6 months notice + 2 minor releases)?
Do we require SDKs to include a runtime-compat 'compat-check' call that Console/CI can exercise pre-rollout?,
What telemetry baseline must be available from Dedicated and Private deployments to safely use the Advisor's automatic health gating?
Should security review gate be mandatory before any manifest entry that relaxes compatibility guarantees?
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Overly strict manifest could block timely security patches. Mitigation: Allow 'emergency' tag in manifest with explicit emergency rollout guidance and required post-fix reconciliation.
Risk: Manifest drift between repos and published binaries. Mitigation: CI validation, release checklist step to update manifest, and a nightly manifest vs artifact scan job.
Risk: Console advisor recommendations mislead inexperienced users. Mitigation: Add explicit confidence score and link to migration playbook; keep initial advisor read-only.
Risk: On-prem customers may not surface required telemetry. Mitigation: Provide a 'manual mode' checklist for customers to follow when telemetry is missing.
implementation_notes: Schema v1 fields: component, lane, supported_range, guaranteed_patch_window_days, incompatible_until, deprecation_notice_weeks, recommended_migration_steps (link), rollback_target, advisor_hints.
CI hook: 'manifest-lint' will run JSON Schema validation and a custom rule that ensures each artifact release has a corresponding manifest entry or an explicit skip-tag with rationale.
Advisor rule engine prototype uses a small DSL: if health_slo < threshold then reduce canary by X or abort; if model_eval_regression > delta then abort and fallback to target-version.
Console integration: Advisor API endpoint will return: recommended_canary_percent, required_checks (list), estimated_risk_score, suggested_rollback_target, links to playbooks.
Migration playbooks will include: pre-upgrade checklist, known incompatibilities and KC steps, telemetry queries to run post-canary, and rollback steps.
next_steps: Resolve open questions with Security, Runtime, and Dedicated teams by 2025-03-07.
Complete Console UI mock review and security checklist; schedule design review with PM and Design by 2025-03-10.
Merge manifest schema v1 after small changes and add CI validation job (owner: eng-infra).
Implement advisor read-only endpoint and wire prototype in Console for the LTS -> Stability upgrade trial during next release window.
